Our results collectively show that stronger and combined antifungal selection redirects genomic responses rather than simply amplifying those favored under less challenging conditions, highlighting the limits of predicting adaptation from simpler selection regimes.

items.title_en: AlphaGenome Enhances Personal Gene Expression Prediction but Retains Key Limitations
items.title_zh: AlphaGenome 提升个体基因表达预测但仍保留关键局限
items.abstract_en: Recent years have seen rapid growth in sequence-to-function (S2F) models that predict diverse molecular readouts from DNA sequence alone. However, these models have faced criticism for their limited accuracy in predicting individual-level gene expression. AlphaGenome, a state-of-the-art S2F model, excels across a range of sequence-based prediction tasks, but its utility for personal expression prediction remains incompletely assessed. Here, we evaluate AlphaGenome's ability to predict tissue-specific, personal gene expression and find that it significantly outperforms its predecessor, Enformer. Across 1,000 genes and 11,471 eligible gene-tissue pairs, AlphaGenome significantly outperforms Enformer for 3,103 pairs, whereas Enformer significantly outperforms AlphaGenome for 828 pairs, yielding a win ratio of 3.75. This imbalance is supported by a global permutation test (P = 2.0e-4), with a median correlation difference of 0.046. Nevertheless, pretrained AlphaGenome substantially underperforms Elastic Net and Random Forest trained on individual-level data. These findings demonstrate that AlphaGenome better captures individual-specific gene expression variation than Enformer, while highlighting substantial room for improvement in sequence-based prediction of personal gene expression.

items.title_en: A high-resolution protein-RNA binding atlas for structure-aware interaction prediction and post-transcriptional regulatory modeling
items.title_zh: 面向结构感知互作预测与转录后调控建模的高分辨率蛋白-RNA结合图谱
items.abstract_en: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) control post-transcriptional gene expression by regulating RNA processing, localization, stability, and translation. However, our understanding of RNA regulation remains limited by the resolution, scale, and uniformity of available RBP binding maps. Here we introduce eclair CLIP (ecCLIP), a high-throughput CLIP-seq platform that combines endogenous protein tagging for uniform affinity capture with ligation-free library preparation to generate high-resolution RNA-protein binding profiles. We applied ecCLIP to 67 endogenously tagged RBPs in HEK293T cells, generating a high-quality transcriptome-scale atlas that recovered known binding preferences and captured post-transcriptional regulons linked to RNA half-life. To test the utility of the atlas, we incorporated ecCLIP into Borzuki, a Borzoi-derived sequence-to-function model trained on complementary RNA degradation, expression, CLIP, and Perturb-seq data. Inclusion of ecCLIP data improved RNA half-life prediction and assessment of 3' UTR variant effects on RNA stability, demonstrating that our atlas helps capture RNA dynamics. To directly model the cis-regulatory grammar underlying these RBP-RNA interactions, we developed Pythia, a structure-aware neural network architecture that incorporates context-free grammar-inspired fixed convolutions to explicitly encode RNA base-pairing features. Pythia predicted RBP binding from sequence and structural context and decomposed predictions into sequence- and structure-dependent components. We tested this decomposition for five RBPs using massively parallel reporter CLIP (MPRC) binding assays in cells, using synthetic RNA libraries containing mutations designed to preserve or disrupt predicted RNA structures across nominated binding sites. We used the same MPRC strategy to confirm allele-specific binding effects for variants prioritized by Pythia. Together, ecCLIP and Pythia provide a resource for structure-aware decoding of RNA-protein interaction grammar and interpretation of post-transcriptional regulatory variation.
items.abstract_zh: RNA结合蛋白（RBP）通过调控RNA加工、定位、稳定性与翻译来控制转录后基因表达，但现有RBP结合图谱在分辨率、规模与一致性上的不足限制了相关研究。本文提出eclair CLIP（ecCLIP）：一种结合内源蛋白标签均一捕获与免连接建库的高通量CLIP-seq平台。作者对HEK293T细胞中67个内源标签RBP作图，获得高质量转录组规模图谱，重现了已知结合偏好，并捕获与RNA半衰期相关的转录后调控子网络。将ecCLIP数据纳入由Borzoi衍生的序列到功能模型Borzuki后，RNA半衰期预测及3' UTR变异对RNA稳定性影响的评估均得到改善。为直接建模RBP-RNA互作的顺式调控语法，作者开发了结构感知神经网络Pythia，利用受无上下文文法启发的固定卷积显式编码RNA碱基配对特征，并将预测分解为序列依赖与结构依赖成分，随后用MPRC实验对五个RBP加以检验。
items.highlight_zh: ecCLIP高通量图谱提升RBP结合预测与RNA稳定性建模
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】RNA结合蛋白（RBP）决定RNA的命运，包括剪接、运输、降解和翻译。要建模这些规则，需要一张覆盖广、分辨率高、批次间一致性好的“RBP—RNA结合地图”。现有CLIP数据在这些方面不足，限制了预测模型的准确性。
【用了什么方法】作者开发eclair CLIP（ecCLIP）：把标签直接加到细胞内源蛋白上，让不同RBP都能用同一套流程高效捕获，并采用免连接（ligation-free）建库以减小偏好和噪声。他们对HEK293T细胞中67个内源标签RBP进行作图；再把图谱数据喂给由Borzoi衍生的序列到功能模型Borzuki；同时开发结构感知神经网络Pythia，用受无上下文文法启发的固定卷积编码RNA二级结构，把结合预测拆分为序列贡献与结构贡献，并用MPRC（大规模并行报告CLIP）实验，以设计好“保结构/破结构”突变的合成RNA库对5个RBP进行验证。
【有什么结果】ecCLIP重现了已知结合偏好，给出了与RNA半衰期相关的调控网络；加入ecCLIP数据后，RNA半衰期预测以及3' UTR变异对稳定性影响的评估都有提升；Pythia能够从序列与结构预测结合，并把预测分解为序列与结构两部分。
【为何重要】一是提供了高质量、可比对的RBP结合资源；二是示范了“实验图谱—序列到功能模型—结构感知预测”的闭环，有助于解释非编码区变异（如3' UTR突变）如何影响RNA稳定性，为RNA药物研发与疾病变异解读提供工具。

items.title_en: Shared genomic signatures of Arctic adaptation among distantly related plant lineages
items.title_zh: 远缘植物谱系间北极适应的共享基因组特征
items.abstract_en: Extreme environments impose strong selection pressures that can drive convergent adaptation among distantly related species. Arctic plants survive low temperatures, 24-hour light in summer and darkness in winter, short growing seasons, limited precipitation, nutrient-poor soils, and extreme seasonal variation. To test if these conditions are associated with shared genomic signatures, we generated a chromosome-level genome assembly for Oxyria digyna and compared it with existing reference genomes for three distantly related Arctic species (Cochlearia groenlandica, Draba nivalis, Dryas octopetala) and for 16 non-Arctic species from the same families. We identified 214 orthogroups with signatures of positive selection in all Arctic species, 1.6 times the number shared among the non-Arctic species. Although no gene ontology (GO) categories remained significantly enriched after multiple-testing correction, descriptive annotations included genes involved in general functions including protein folding, glycolysis, transcription, and oxidative-stress responses. Orthogroups showing copy number variation were associated with biotic interactions, sexual reproduction, and nutrient acquisition, suggesting that species may respond to biotic and nutrient stresses by shifts in gene copy number. Arctic and alpine genomes contained lower proportions of some repetitive elements, including terminal inverted repeats, and smaller regions of centromeric repeats than non-Arctic genomes. Overall, we see shared genes under positive selection, similar functions of genes with high copy number variation, and lower counts of some repetitive elements in the Arctic plant genomes. Our findings reveal a shared genomic signature of Arctic adaptation across deeply diverged plant lineages, suggesting that evolution in extreme environments repeatedly targets similar genomic features.

items.title_en: Sensitive period for song learning outlasts parent-offspring cohesion in wild zebra finches
items.title_zh: 野生斑胸草雀的鸣唱学习敏感期长于亲子凝聚期
items.abstract_en: Communication is central to social behaviour, with vocalisations playing a crucial role in many species. In some species, vocalisations are learned, with songbirds being key to understanding vocal learning. The Australian zebra finch (Taeniopygia castanotis) is the most studied model organism for vocal learning. In captivity, juveniles are typically housed with their father, where males learn their father song and females develop a preference for that song. In nature, however, the social structure of zebra finches is more dynamic across space and time. To identify the natural social conditions during song learning, we followed zebra finch families across their early life in the wild using automated radio-tracking. The distance between juveniles and their parents increased post-fledging and became similar to the distance between juveniles and unrelated adults by the second half of the song learning period. These findings indicate a highly dynamic social environment during the song learning period and suggest that juvenile males could learn from many tutors and that females may develop broader song preferences. Thus, studies based on one-tutor paradigms should be interpreted carefully with respect to functional implications and highlight that future vocal learning studies could better reflect the social conditions under which song develops.

items.title_en: Identification and inhibition of the Cyclin D Rb-docking interface that drives cell division
items.title_zh: 驱动细胞分裂的 Cyclin D–Rb 对接界面的鉴定与抑制
items.abstract_en: The animal cell division cycle is initiated by the cyclin-dependent kinases CDK4 and CDK6 in complex with D-type cyclins. Cyclin D-CDK4/6 complex formation is promoted by the assembly factors p21 and p27, which bind both subunits. p27 binds the hydrophobic patch on cyclin D that is similar to the patch used by other cell cycle cyclins to dock their substrates. This raised the question as to how cyclin D could find its substrates if its hydrophobic patch were already occupied? Here, we show that D-type cyclins use their A2' helix to dock the retinoblastoma protein Rb, a key substrate regulating cell cycle progression. The specific interface of cyclin D's A2' helix is unique among cyclins and its mutation slows proliferation. Taken together, our work identifies a cyclin D-substrate docking mechanism that can be targeted by novel cancer therapeutics.

items.title_en: A High-Sensitivity and High-Throughput LC-MS Workflow for Low-Input and Single-Cell Proteomics
items.title_zh: 用于低输入和单细胞蛋白质组学的高灵敏度、高通量 LC-MS 工作流程
items.abstract_en: Single-cell proteomics (SCP) requires sample preparation that minimizes sample loss and highly sensitive LC-MS analysis because the amount of protein available from a single cell is extremely limited. Here, we developed an integrated workflow for low-input and single-cell proteomics based on single-cell proteomics by LMNG-assisted sample preparation (scpLASP), which enables microliter-scale sample preparation using standard laboratory consumables. Systematic optimization of peptide reconstitution conditions identified 0.01% n-dodecyl-{beta}-D-maltoside (DDM) combined with 0.01% lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG) as the condition yielding the highest number of identified peptides among those tested for low-input samples. Optimization of the LC mobile-phase composition identified 0.5% acetic acid with 1% dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) as the optimal condition, increasing the mean number of identified protein groups from 6,767 with 0.1% formic acid to 7,409 for 250 pg HeLa digests analyzed using an Orbitrap Astral Zoom. Shortening the LC gradient from 11 to 5.5 min enabled higher analytical throughput while maintaining mean identification counts of 6,558 and 7,088 protein groups from 100 and 250 pg HeLa digests, respectively, with median protein-level coefficients of variation of 9.20% and 6.99%. When the optimized workflow was applied to HEK293-derived Expi293F single cells using the same 5.5-min LC gradient, an effective analytical throughput of 135 samples per day was achieved with an injection volume of 4.5 {micro}L, accounting for sample-loading time. This workflow identified a median of 5,655 protein groups per cell using an empirical spectral library generated from 20-cell samples. Overall, this study establishes a sensitive and high-throughput workflow for low-input and single-cell proteomics that combines low-loss microliter-scale sample preparation with optimized LC-MS analysis, achieving high proteome depth and analytical throughput without requiring specialized nanoliter-scale sample-preparation devices.

items.title_en: Scooby-2: fine-tuning AlphaGenome for single-cell genomic track prediction
items.title_zh: Scooby-2：微调 AlphaGenome 用于单细胞基因组轨迹预测
items.abstract_en: Sequence-to-function models predict genomic tracks from DNA sequence. AlphaGenome has been shown to outperform previous models, including Borzoi, on most track-prediction and variant-effect benchmarks. However, like its predecessors, it predicts tracks only for predefined, mostly bulk-derived cell types and tissues. While Scooby has extended Borzoi to single-cell resolution, a single-cell adaptation of AlphaGenome is still lacking. We present Scooby-2, which combines AlphaGenome with a cell-specific decoder to predict single-cell RNA-seq coverage and chromatin-accessibility genomic tracks from DNA sequence. The package provides the implementation, the parameter-efficient fine-tuning setup, the training pipeline and inference scripts. When evaluated on the NeurIPS bone marrow single-cell dataset, Scooby-2 achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.56 when predicting cell-type-specific gene expression differences, compared with 0.53 for Scooby. When using the distilled AlphaGenome backbone, variant effect prediction concordance of fine-mapped eQTLs from the OneK1K cohort improved from 0.37 to 0.47 Spearman's rank correlation across all associations, an improvement consistent with that of AlphaGenome over Borzoi itself.

items.title_en: Joint localization and testing reveals spatial context of differential expression
items.title_zh: 联合定位与检验揭示差异表达的空间情境
items.abstract_en: Multi-subject spatial transcriptomics is increasingly used to identify molecular differences across individuals and conditions while resolving where in tissue those differences occur. Yet subject-level differential expression (DE) analyses commonly require spatial regions to be specified in advance, separating localization from testing. Here we present SpaceDX, a framework that uses gene-specific attention-based spatial weighting to jointly test differential expression and localize the spatial expression patterns contributing to these associations. In simulations, SpaceDX outperforms cluster-based DE methods when differential expression does not align with predefined spatial boundaries. Across two multi-subject mouse brain datasets, SpaceDX detected 45.8% more DE genes than regional DESeq2 pseudobulk in a chronic stress model, while in an Alzheimer's disease model combining SpaceDX with DESeq2 increased discovery by 19.1% relative to DESeq2 alone. Across both datasets, the learned maps provided spatial context for condition-associated expression signals in addition to gene-level significance. In the chronic stress model, for example, oligodendrocyte- and myelin-associated genes showed shared localization to corresponding brain structures. Together, these results show that the spatial context of differential expression can be inferred jointly with gene-level associations, recovering signals obscured by regional aggregation without requiring the relevant tissue context to be defined in advance.

items.title_en: MutQA: A Cross-Validated Q&A Dataset for Genetic Mutations
items.title_zh: MutQA：一个用于遗传突变的交叉验证问答数据集
items.abstract_en: We introduce MutQA, a dataset of 330,387 citation-grounded question-answer (QA) pairs linking genetic mutations to their functional consequences as described in the biomedical literature. Each record pairs a protein-coding mutation with a natural-language question and an evidence-backed answer anchored to sentences in one of 27,442 open-access PubMed Central articles, spanning 6,620 genes and 125,593 gene-variant pairs. The dataset is constructed using CrossValQA, a framework that enforces information isolation between independent LLMs: one model generates QA pairs from an article, a second model answers the same question without access to the first model's response, and a third model judges whether each model's rationale supports the other's answer, so that retained QA pairs are reproducible from the source text rather than hallucinated. Of 401,406 audited QA pairs, 82.7% pass both directions of this cross-validation; those with a recoverable reference protein sequence form the released benchmark. In a 999-pair stratified audit, two expert annotators agree exactly on 86.4% of cross-validated QA pairs (95% CI 83.7-89.0; n = 638), a tier in which about 90% of ratings are "correct". Individual LLM judges agree with individual annotators at a comparable 87.0% on this tier but far less on QA pairs that fail cross-validation. Fine-tuning MutaPLM on MutQA nearly doubles its mean LLM-judge score for question-conditioned mutation-effect answering (1.45 to 2.82 on a 0-5 scale) and improves mutation-recovery accuracy from effect descriptions from 19.4% to 32.1%. Providing variant-matched MutQA retrieval context, without fine-tuning, improves strict answer accuracy across four LLM families by 20.0-28.6 percentage points, demonstrating the framework's ability to improve the reliability of LLM answers. We also apply CrossValQA to proteomics, providing a proof of concept for its use beyond mutation-specific QA. We release the dataset, construction framework, and evaluation code.

items.title_en: WITHDRAWN: PD-L2 Regulates Natural Antibody and IL-10 Secretion by B-1 cells
items.title_zh: 已撤回：PD-L2 调节 B-1 细胞的天然抗体和 IL-10 分泌
items.abstract_en: The authors have withdrawn this manuscript because of concerns regarding the reliability of the data. Therefore, the authors do not wish this work to be cited as reference for the project. If you have any questions, please contact the corresponding author.

items.title_en: Efficient biological design via genomic in-context learning
items.title_zh: 通过基因组上下文学习实现高效生物设计
items.abstract_en: In-context learning (ICL), the ability to perform new tasks from a few examples supplied in a prompt, is a defining emergent capability of large language models. Here, we show that ICL emerges in the genome language model Evo 2 and enables biological design. With as few as four examples in the prompt and no additional training, Evo 2 generates realistic metal-binding proteins, de novo antibodies, protein-RNA systems, and entire bacteriophage genomes. For {Phi}X174-like bacteriophage design, ICL surpasses previously fine-tuned models on computational measures of design quality and diversity. Beyond {Phi}X174, conditioning the model with different phage prompts enables us to efficiently design MS2 and M13 genomes in silico without fine-tuning. Iteratively updating the prompt with newly generated phage genomes, which we refer to as genomic chain-of-thought, further improves the diversity of designs while maintaining quality metrics. Paired with an inference engine that accelerates generation up to 35-fold and extends practicable context to a megabase, these results establish ICL as a versatile and efficient paradigm for biological sequence design.
items.abstract_zh: 上下文学习（ICL），即仅凭提示中给出的少量示例完成新任务的能力，是大语言模型的标志性涌现能力。本文表明，ICL在基因组语言模型Evo 2中出现，并可用于生物设计。提示中仅需四个示例、无需额外训练，Evo 2即可生成逼真的金属结合蛋白、从头抗体、蛋白-RNA系统乃至完整的噬菌体基因组。在ΦX174类噬菌体设计中，ICL在设计质量与多样性的计算指标上超过了此前经过微调的模型。除ΦX174外，以不同噬菌体提示进行条件化，可在无需微调的情况下于计算机中高效设计MS2与M13基因组。用新生成的噬菌体基因组迭代更新提示（作者称之为基因组思维链）可进一步提升设计多样性并保持质量指标。配合可将生成速度提升最高35倍、并把可用上下文扩展至1兆碱基的推理引擎，这些结果确立了ICL作为一种通用、高效的生物序列设计范式。
items.highlight_zh: Evo 2凭少量示例涌现上下文学习，免微调设计噬菌体基因组
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】大语言模型具有“上下文学习（ICL）”能力：不修改参数，只在提示里给几个例子就能完成新任务。那么，基因组语言模型Evo 2是否也具备这种能力？它能否被直接用于设计生物序列？
【用了什么方法】作者在Evo 2上进行提示实验：只给4个示例、完全不做微调，让它生成蛋白质与基因组序列；把ICL与专门微调过的模型在计算指标上比较；还提出“基因组思维链”，也就是把新生成的噬菌体基因组回填到提示中反复迭代，以提升多样性；并配套开发了推理引擎，使生成速度最高提升35倍、可用上下文扩展至1 Mb。
【有什么结果】模型生成了逼真的金属结合蛋白、从头抗体、蛋白-RNA系统和完整噬菌体基因组；在ΦX174类噬菌体设计中，ICL在设计质量与多样性上超过此前的微调模型；换用不同噬菌体提示，还能在计算机内高效设计MS2与M13基因组；迭代更新提示能进一步提升多样性，同时保持质量指标。
【为何重要】这表明ICL是基因组模型的一种涌现能力，为生物设计提供了“少样本、免训练、通用”的新范式：只需更换提示就能切换设计任务，省去为每个目标重新训练模型的成本。同时也提示，应关注这类能力带来的生物安全与监管议题。

items.title_en: Plasma Proteogenomics Identifies RGMB as a Candidate for Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma Detected Only in East Asians
items.title_zh: 血浆蛋白质基因组学鉴定出 RGMB 是仅在东亚人群中检测到的原发性开角型青光眼候选因子
items.abstract_en: Purpose: In East Asians most primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) occurs at statistically normal intraocular pressure (IOP). We sought plasma proteins linked to POAG through genetic signal not shared with IOP. Methods: We integrated the BioBank Japan POAG GWAS with a Japanese plasma pQTL resource (Nagahama; SomaScan v4) using SMR/HEIDI and colocalization against POAG and IOP datasets, including a Genomic-SEM-derived non-IOP POAG component, adding a symmetric proteome-wide cross-ancestry colocalization, fine-mapping and multi-signal colocalization of the RGMB region, a formal heterogeneity test, and expression mapping in retina and trabecular meshwork. Results: Of 679 plasma proteins, four colocalized with POAG in East Asians only, five in Europeans only, none in both. SMR nominated RGMB as a suggestive risk factor (b_SMR = +0.277; HEIDI P > 0.05; PP4 = 0.684; rs1037599); none survived Bonferroni correction. RGMB did not colocalize with European IOP, a European non-IOP POAG component, or European POAG on the same platform, despite a common, directionally consistent pQTL instrument. Multi-signal colocalization reproduced both the East Asian signal and the European null. The per-allele POAG effect differed between ancestries (Cochran's Q P = 0.0036; I2 = 88%), the better-powered European data excluding an effect of East Asian magnitude. RGMB and its receptors were expressed in trabecular meshwork cells and unchanged by TGF-beta2. Conclusions: This triangulation nominates the RGMB-neogenin-BMP axis as a POAG candidate detected in East Asians but not Europeans, which does not colocalize with IOP-related traits. The findings are exploratory; ancestry-matched replication and functional validation are required.

items.title_en: Multi-ancestry genome-wide and transcriptome-wide association analyses identify new risk loci and genes for inflammatory bowel disease
items.title_zh: 多祖源全基因组和全转录组关联分析识别炎症性肠病的新风险位点和基因
items.abstract_en: To advance genetic understanding of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we conduct multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) meta-analyses of 63,415 cases of Europeans and East Asians, and identified 60 previously unreported susceptibility loci. Integrating multi-ancestry transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), cell type-specific TWAS, alternative splicing, and alternative polyadenylation analyses using RNA-sequencing data from normal colon tissues of 707 Europeans and 364 East Asians, we identify 441 candidate risk genes, including 324 not previously implicated by GWAS or TWAS, of which 291 were further supported by colocalization or summary-data-based Mendelian randomization analyses. These genes converge on pathways central to IBD pathogenesis (e.g., immune regulation), with over half showing transcriptional dysregulation supported by single-cell and spatial omics analyses. We further identify 44 druggable genes linked to 221 approved drugs or Phase II/III clinical-stage compounds. Our findings deepen the understanding of IBD genetics and provide insights for future research relevant to precision medicine for IBD.

items.title_en: Single-cell genetics identifies cell-type-specific effector genes across complex traits and diseases
items.abstract_en: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been instrumental in uncovering the genetic basis of complex traits. When integrated with expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping, they can help identify effector genes within GWAS loci through gene regulatory mechanisms. Recent single-cell eQTL (sc-eQTL) studies suggest that genetic effects on gene expression are often cell type- and subtype-specific, providing opportunities to uncover context-specific roles of effector genes that may be obscured in traditional GWAS and eQTL studies in bulk tissues. Here, we leverage results from sc-eQTL mapping in the TenK10K phase 1 project to prioritise effector genes across 69 diseases and 31 biomarker traits, from a total of 12,266 eGenes identified in 28 peripheral immune cell types. Using Mendelian randomisation (MR) and colocalisation, we present a catalogue of predicted effector genes and their estimated directional effects on the trait at cell type resolution, spanning 54,245 associations across 5,270 genes and 28 cell types for disease traits, and 348,103 associations across 9,581 genes and 28 cell types for biomarker traits. By quantifying polygenic enrichment at both the single-cell and cell type levels, we identify distinct immune cell contributions to both immune-related and systemic conditions. We demonstrate differential polygenic enrichment of Crohn's disease and COVID-19 amongst dendritic cell subtypes. Integration with clinical drug development data reveals that therapeutic compounds targeting gene-trait associations identified in this study are twice as likely to have secured regulatory approval. Using Crohn's disease as a motivating example, we demonstrate how population-based sc-eQTL data can pinpoint risk loci, effector genes and cell types, complementing findings from disease-focused tissue samples. Our findings provide a foundational resource for understanding the cell-type-specific genetic architecture of disease and for guiding therapeutic discovery.

items.title_en: Unravelling the genetic basis of stuttering: GWAS meta-analysis highlights link with rare speech disorders
items.abstract_en: Developmental stuttering affects up to 11% of children, with around one-fifth developing a persistent stutter. Twin and family studies indicate a strong genetic contribution and comorbidity with other heritable traits, but the common genetic architecture of clinically ascertained stuttering, persistence and recovery remains poorly characterised. We performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis of 6,096 cases and 81,629 controls of European ancestries from 18 cohorts, including 2,953 cases from stuttering-specific collections with clinically confirmed or validated self-reported phenotypes. We additionally analysed persistence, severity and frequency, and integrated our results with an independent GWAS of self-reported stuttering. Our meta-analysis and the self-report GWAS showed high genetic correlation (rg = 0.66). A polygenic score from the self-report GWAS was associated with stuttering in our ascertained cases, with modest predictive value ({Delta}AUC = 0.067, p = 1.8 x 10-23), and with greater severity and frequency among people who stutter. We replicated two self-report loci (CAMTA1, CTNND2), and combined analysis identified a genome-wide significant association at MPPED2. Our 24 suggestive loci implicated genes with established roles in childhood apraxia of speech, including SETBP1, CAMTA1, PTBP2, GRIN2A and KIRREL3, with strong enrichment for apraxia genes (OR = 40.1, p = 1 x 10-4). Within our meta-analysis, persistent stuttering was genetically near-identical to stuttering overall (rg = 0.97). Genetically predicted brain imaging nominally implicated basal ganglia and cerebellar motor circuitry. Common-variant liability to stuttering is shared across ascertainment approaches, relates to severity, and converges with rare-variant genes for speech disorders on circuits underlying speech motor control.

items.title_en: Deep learning-based electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior myocardial infarction: explainability, human-AI interaction, and a utilization bias hypothesis
items.abstract_en: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) may improve electrocardiographic differentiation of Takotsubo syndrome from acute anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), but its impact on human diagnostic performance, the added value of visual explanations, and differences by reader background and experience remain uncertain. Methods: Using 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) images from two hospitals, we developed and externally validated an ensemble of three deep learning models after self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning. The diagnostic task used ECGs recorded within 14 days after symptom onset, regardless of reperfusion status. We conducted a four-phase reader study. Phases 1-3 compared unaided interpretation, a reference sheet, and additional AI assistance. In Phase 4, readers evaluated a new ECG set after randomization to reference-sheet support alone, with AI predictions, or with AI predictions plus gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) heatmaps. Diagnostic correctness was analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models. Exploratory analyses examined differences by cardiologist status and experience. Results: Development and external-validation cohorts, including healthy controls, comprised 832 and 95 participants, respectively. For Takotsubo-STEMI discrimination, external-validation accuracy was 0.914, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic and precision-recall curves of 0.970 and 0.984. Seventy healthcare providers completed the reader study. The estimated probability of correct diagnosis increased from 0.632 without assistance to 0.864 with AI assistance (odds ratio [OR], 3.71; P<0.001). In randomized Phase 4, AI assistance improved accuracy vs reference-sheet support alone (OR, 4.28; 95% CI, 3.08-5.95; P<0.001), and Grad-CAM provided additional benefit (OR, 1.53; 95% CI, 1.04-2.25; P=0.033). Exploratory analyses showed greater improvement among less experienced readers; with AI assistance, non-cardiologists outperformed cardiologists. AI-assisted readers remained less accurate overall than the model alone. Conclusions: An ECG image-based ensemble differentiated Takotsubo syndrome from anterior STEMI and improved reader accuracy. Visual explanations provided additional benefit, while experience-related differences highlight the importance of effective human-AI interaction.

items.title_en: CSF Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers in Relation to Functional Status and Tofersen Treatment Response in ALS
items.abstract_en: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a neurodegenerative disease primarily affecting motor neurons but also frequently involving cognitive impairment. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) measurements of {beta} amyloid peptides (A{beta}40, A{beta}42), tau proteins, and neurofilaments are clinically established biomarkers in neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (AD). Emerging evidence suggests that AD-related pathological changes and AD-related biomarkers may appear in ALS, yet their diagnostic and prognostic significance remains unclear. In this retrospective study, we analyzed clinical and CSF biomarker data from patients with ALS, AD, Huntington's disease (HD), and other disease controls recruited in a real-world clinical setting. The dataset comprised A{beta}40, A{beta}42, total tau (t-Tau), phosphorylated tau181 (pTau181), phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNfH), and relevant serum markers. Additionally, longitudinal CSF sampling over one year was evaluated in three ALS patients receiving tofersen treatment. In this real-world cohort, AD-related CSF biomarkers demonstrated no diagnostic value for distinguishing ALS from other neurodegenerative conditions. However, A{beta}40, A{beta}42, and pTau181 levels correlated positively with ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) global score and serum Creatine Kinase MB (CK-MB) concentrations. At the same time, a higher A{beta}42/A{beta}40 ratio was associated with better memory performance on the Edinburgh Cognitive and Behavioural ALS Screen (ECAS). In tofersen-treated cases, AD-related biomarkers gradually declined during follow-up. These findings suggest that elevated CSF AD-associated biomarkers in ALS may reflect preserved functional and cognitive status and exhibited parallel declines during follow-up in three tofersen-treated patients, supporting their further prospective evaluation as exploratory markers of therapeutic responsiveness.

items.title_en: PharmaAgent: a real-world evaluation of high- and low-autonomy agentic systems for inpatient vancomycin dosing
items.abstract_en: Vancomycin has a narrow therapeutic window requiring individualized dosing and repeated monitoring, a process health systems delegate from physicians to pharmacists for consistency. We silently deployed PharmaAgent, LLM-based vancomycin dosing agentic systems, at Stanford Hospital for two months and compared high- and low-autonomy configurations, each with and without institutional guidelines. Across 403 dosing events in 316 patients, mean absolute percentage error against the treating pharmacist's order was 21.8% with high autonomy versus 37.8% with low autonomy, and recommendations were within 25% of the order in 73.4% versus 50.9% of events (P < 0.001); a second pharmacist was within 25% in 90.2%. Pharmacist review of 196 out-of-tolerance recommendations found a safety concern in 65.8%, more often with low autonomy (odds ratio 2.37). A higher-autonomy agent that self-debugged its intermediate steps proved more robust than stricter engineering, but neither configuration is ready to dose patients without pharmacist oversight.

items.title_en: Long Sleep and Insomnia are Associated with Reduced Global Cognitive Function across Diverse Populations
items.abstract_en: Background: Although sleep disorders are generally associated with cognitive decline, definitions of sleep conditions and cognitive function vary greatly across studies. Therefore, we evaluated associations between consensus definitions of sleep and cognitive outcomes across multiple studies. Methods: Consensus sleep measures were ascertained at baseline visits in three cohort studies (HCHS/SOL, MESA and ARIC, N=11,563): short and long sleep ([≤]6hours and [≥]9hours), insomnia (Women's Health Initiative Insomnia Rating Scale [≥]10 or [≥]6 for 3 questions), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness [≥]11) and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA, Apnea-Hypopnea Index [≥]15). Cognitive measures were ascertained at baseline and follow-up visits in each study and used to calculate harmonized outcomes: global cognitive function (GCF) at baseline, change in GCF between baseline and follow-up, poor GCF at baseline ([≥]1SD below the median), and incident poor GCF at follow-up. Study-specific analyses were adjusted for age, sex, center, education, race/ethnicity, APOE4 and language of cognitive assessments as needed. Results were meta-analyzed across studies. Results: Long sleep was consistently associated with lower baseline GCF ({beta}=-0.19, SE=0.03, p=3.78x10-14, FDR p=7.56x10-13, p-heterogeneity=0.78) and increased odds of poor baseline GCF (OR=1.77, 95% CI=1.49-2.09, p=2.96x10-11, FDR p=2.96x10-10, p-heterogeneity=0.22) across cohorts. Insomnia was also suggestively associated with lower baseline GCF ({beta}=-0.051, SE=0.02, p=0.01, FDR p=0.07, p-heterogeneity=0.005) and increased odds of poor baseline GCF (OR=1.22, 95% CI=1.06-1.41, p=6.76x10-3, FDR p=0.05, p-heterogeneity=0.03). Sleep measures were not associated with change in cognitive function. Discussion: Associations of long sleep and insomnia with harmonized cross-sectional GCF across three large, multiethnic cohorts suggest that cognitive function may be associated with distinct sleep phenotypes.

items.title_en: Comparative Risk of Suicide-Related Events Across Antidepressant Classes in Autistic Individuals: A New-User Active Comparator Cohort Study
items.abstract_en: IntroductionComparative evidence on suicide-related outcomes across antidepressant treatments among autistic individuals is limited. We examined associations between antidepressant treatment class and suicide-related events (SREs) among individuals on the autism spectrum initiating antidepressants. MethodsWe conducted a retrospective new-user, active-comparator cohort study using the nationwide Truveta database of electronic health records. Autistic individuals initiating antidepressants after an autism spectrum diagnosis were classified by initial treatment as a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), atypical antidepressant, serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI), or tricyclic antidepressant (TCA). Pairwise propensity score overlap weighting was used to balance baseline characteristics, and associations with SREs during as-treated follow-up were estimated using weighted Cox proportional hazards models. ResultsAmong 42,441 autistic antidepressant initiators, atypical antidepressants (hazard ratio [HR], 0.787; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.632-0.979) and TCAs (HR, 0.487; 95% CI, 0.263-0.902) were associated with lower observed SRE hazards compared with SSRIs, whereas no clear difference was observed for SNRIs (HR, 0.948; 95% CI, 0.651-1.381). In agent-specific analyses, trazodone was associated with a lower observed SRE hazard compared with SSRIs, whereas no clear differences were observed for bupropion or mirtazapine. Exploratory age-stratified analyses suggested a lower hazard for atypical antidepressants versus SSRIs among individuals younger than 18 years, although evidence of effect modification was not consistent across alternative specifications of age. DiscussionAmong autistic individuals initiating antidepressants, observed SRE hazards differed across some antidepressant treatment comparisons. The class-level association for atypical antidepressants was not observed consistently across its individual agents, and age-related differences warrant further investigation. Lay SummaryAutistic people are often treated with antidepressants, but little is known about whether different types of antidepressants are associated with different effects on reducing the onsets of suicide-related events. In this large real-world study, we compared several commonly used antidepressant treatments among autistic individuals and found that some treatment groups had lower observed rates of suicide-related events than others, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously because treatment choice may reflect differences between patients that cannot be fully measured in health records. The findings may help inform future research on the safety of antidepressant treatment in autistic people.

items.title_en: Why Americans Choose Raw Milk: Evidence from a National Quantitative Survey
items.abstract_en: Raw milk consumption is a controllable source of foodborne pathogen exposure in the United States (US), yet existing national estimates of raw milk consumption behaviors are outdated and do not capture emerging factors such as consumers' trusted information sources, sociopolitical influences, and at-home risk mitigation behaviors. We conducted a nationally representative cross-sectional survey of n=1078 US adults to estimate the prevalence of raw milk consumption and at-home thermal treatment practices and identify predictors of these behaviors. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate predictors of raw milk consumption and thermal treatment behavior using adjusted odds ratios (aORs). Among 1,075 eligible respondents, 15% consumed raw milk in the last six months, including 5% exclusively and 10% in addition to pasteurized milk. In multivariable analysis, raw milk consumption was independently associated with younger age, cohabitation with high-risk individuals for foodborne infections (including children less than or equal to five years of age, and elderly, pregnant or immunocompromised individuals) who had consumed raw milk, and perceptions of raw milk taste and safety. Adults aged greater than or equal to 55 years had lower odds of consumption than those aged 18-24 years (aOR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02-0.15), while those living with a high-risk household member who consumed raw milk had higher odds of consumption (aOR, 4.39; 95% CI, 2.69-7.22). Perceiving raw milk to have higher risk of causing illness was associated with lower odds of raw milk consumption (aOR: 0.32, 95% CI: 0.17-0.62) compared to believing the risk to be equal across milk types, and thermal treatment was reported by 38% of exclusive raw milk consumers (n=58) and 47% of consumers of both milk types (n=106). Raw milk consumption in the US appears to be substantially more common than previously reported and shaped by factors such as taste, safety, and household raw milk consumption among high-risk individuals for foodborne infections. The proportion of raw milk consumers already practicing at-home thermal treatment suggests a potential opportunity for risk mitigation.

items.title_en: IG-28 enables identification and quantification of high-confidence isoforms from large bulk and single-cell full-length cDNA datasets
items.title_zh: IG-28能够从大规模bulk和单细胞全长cDNA数据集中识别和定量高置信度异构体
items.abstract_en: The technology to sequence full-length transcriptomes from bulk and single-cell samples has rapidly advanced. As a result, full-length cDNA datasets now reach billions of reads in size which is beyond the capability of most established isoform identification tools. Here, we introduce IG-28 which addresses this challenge with its capability to process and analyze large fl-cDNA datasets fast and using minimal computational resources. In contrast to its predecessor Mandalorion, IG-28 is not limited to bulk fl-cDNA but is capable of parsing, processing, and analyzing single-cell fl-cDNA datasets. It does so in a lightweight, flexible manner, integrating seamlessly with established scRNA-seq analysis workflows. We benchmarked IG-28 against a variety of established and new isoform identification tools using several bulk and a complex single-cell fl-cDNA dataset and found that IG-28 consistently outperformed the other tools by identifying high-confidence public isoforms.

items.title_en: Arena3D 3.0: a web server for exploring, analyzing, annotating and sharing multilayered networks in 3D
items.title_zh: Arena3D 3.0：用于在3D中探索、分析、注释和共享多层网络的Web服务器
items.abstract_en: Multilayer networks describe biological entities linked by several kinds of relation or measured under several conditions. Arena3D 3.0, a complete reimplementation of Arena3Dweb, gives each layer its own place in an interactive 3D scene. Networks are uploaded or imported from STRING, IntAct, OmniPath, NDEx, Reactome and the Gene Ontology. Twelve layouts, seven in 3D, are available, and node copies can be aligned across layers. Layers are drawn as floors or 3D containers in thirteen arrangements, including 3D hive plots. Communities and annotated groups can be laid out apart and outlined as hulls or fog clouds, and edges can be bundled. Analyses cover node and multilayer metrics, distributions and perturbation, with chord, Sankey, heatmap, UpSet and UMAP views. Networks go to Cytoscape, Gephi Lite, NORMA and JBrowse 2, gene lists to Flame, and a REST API gives programmatic access. Arena3D 3.0 is free at www.arena3d.org without login.

items.title_en: Rugnux: from diffraction images to structure at synchrotrons and XFELs in one program
items.title_zh: Rugnux：在一个程序中实现从同步辐射和XFELs的衍射图像到结构
items.abstract_en: Rising data rates in macromolecular crystallography outpace multi-program pipelines on computing clusters. Rugnux, a single GPU-accelerated program, turns rotation or serial still diffraction images into merged data and an initial structure. At synchrotrons, results arrive seconds after the last image; on one workstation, 207 public datasets from 36 sources took a median of 15 s each, with deposition-quality. Serial XFEL data were processed faster than the collection rate, enabling real-time structure determination.

items.title_en: AN INTEGRATED HEART-ON-A-CHIP NAM RESOLVES DISTINCT CLINICAL PHENOTYPES OF MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA-REPERFUSION INJURY
items.title_zh: 集成心脏芯片NAM可区分心肌缺血-再灌注损伤的不同临床表型
items.abstract_en: Background: Reperfusion is required for myocardial salvage yet itself injures the heart, and cardioprotective interventions that reduce infarct size experimentally have repeatedly failed to improve outcomes in patients. These interventions are evaluated against viability or infarct size alone, whereas ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury produces structural, biochemical, and contractile dysfunction in the same tissue. No in vitro new approach methodology (NAM), however, resolves all three within one system. Methods: A NAM was created within a heart-on-a-chip platform, which was constructed by culturing neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) on muscular thin films. Cardiomyocytes were subjected to normoxia, 2 hours of ischemia, and ischemia followed by 2 hours of reperfusion. Sarcomeric architecture was quantified by immunofluorescence, cardiomyocyte injury by LIVE/DEAD staining and cardiac troponin I release into conditioned media, while contractile stress and spontaneous beat frequency were recorded on the same films before and after each condition. Results: Under ischemia, z-line density decreased while architectural metrics were preserved, indicating cell loss rather than sarcomere disorganization. Furthermore, viability decreased, troponin elevated, and every contractile stress component declined, while spontaneous beat frequency was unchanged. Reperfusion fractured this uniform depression. Cell death and troponin release increased further, yet structure was unchanged from ischemia, so every functional change occurred on a depleted but architecturally intact cardiomyocyte population. Systolic stress recovered partially, whereas diastolic stress exceeded baseline, leaving active stress suppressed despite oxygen recovery. Beat frequency increased with pronounced variability. Conclusions: This heart-on-a-chip NAM resolved structural, biochemical, and contractile injury that global indices conflate, distinguishing ischemic from reperfusion pathophysiology. Interestingly, individual readouts corresponded to distinct clinical syndromes of ischemic injury, positioning this platform for future testing of cardioprotective candidates against the full injury phenotype.

items.title_en: Metabolic and transcriptional responses reveal co-option of symbiotic processes during early soybean-soybean cyst nematode interaction
items.title_zh: 代谢与转录响应揭示大豆-大豆胞囊线虫早期互作期间共生过程的征用
items.abstract_en: The biochemical mechanisms by which virulent populations of soybean cyst nematode (Heterodera glycines, SCN) overcome host resistance are critical to understanding this economically important pathogen. Here, we deployed metabolic and transcriptome profiling of soybean roots during the SCN infection and establishment process to investigate the molecular and biochemical mechanisms of pathogen establishment. Across samples from a time series spanning nematode invasion to syncytium maturation, we demonstrate that compatible SCN infection does not bypass host immunity but systematically remodels it. In a compatible interaction between soybean carrying the high-copy Rhg1 resistance locus challenged with HG Type 2.5.7 SCN virulent on this host, we identify a 72-metabolite defense signature spanning isoflavonoids, triterpenoid saponins, and phenylpropanoids that persist across all infection stages. Despite activation of this metabolic defense signature by the pathogen on infection, defense transcription is near silence by 3 days post-infection, while defense metabolites persist, revealing a critical decoupling of transcriptional and metabolic defense programs at the precise window of syncytium initiation. Suppression of phenylpropanoid accumulation occurs downstream of PAL transcription, indicating a block at the metabolic level invisible to transcriptomics alone. By 5 days post-infection, cytokinin accumulation coincides with nodulin gene induction and phospholipid remodeling consistent with activation of the legume symbiosis program during syncytium maturation. Together, these findings establish that compatibility arises not from failed recognition but from progressive immune dismantling, including suppression of defense chemistry and co-option of the legume-rhizobium symbiosis machinery.

items.title_en: Iron sensing modules participate in rhizospheric pH perception in rice
items.title_zh: 铁感知模块参与水稻根际pH感知
items.abstract_en: Rhizospheric pH has emerged as one of the most important environmental factors regulating plant fitness in almost every aspect of plant physiology and development. Interestingly, the information on how plant perceive rhizospheric pH is still not well understood. In this report we have elucidated the intricate mechanism where rhizospheric pH mediated changes in relative Fe availability are sensed by the plants to initiate complex physiological responses. Using root specific RNA-seq, ICPMS, hormone quantification and physiological validation in rice, the study revealed Fe availability to be a critical determinant of rhizospheric pH where the relative Fe toxicity towards acidic pH and Fe deficiency towards alkaline pH is deduced by the plant in the form of JA-auxin crosstalk regulating the physiological responses against rhizospheric pH.

items.title_en: Co-transcriptomic network analysis of host-parasite interactions reveals genes underpinning parasite fitness
items.title_zh: 宿主-寄生虫互作的共转录网络分析揭示支撑寄生虫适应度的基因
items.abstract_en: Interactions between parasites and their host organisms generate continuous variation in infection outcomes. Although dual transcriptome studies have demonstrated extensive molecular dialogues between interacting species, it is still unclear how natural variation in host and parasite gene regulatory networks and coordination between them contribute to diverse disease phenotypes. Here, we re-contextualized co-transcriptomes from recombinant inbred lines of the plant-parasitic root-knot nematode Meloidogyne hapla infecting Medicago truncatula host plants with relative measures of infection intensity as a proxy for parasite load. We used infection intensity to estimate interaction gradients on gene expression by calculating its covariance with transcript levels. Quantitative analyses of interaction gradients for host and parasite transcriptomes identified major differences in development-related transcriptional programs along the infection continuum. In addition, integrated network analyses connected host cell wall remodeling with parasite protein production and secretion. Silencing of candidate root-knot nematode genes reduced host galling and parasite reproductive fitness, providing experimental support for our network-derived predictions. Together, our findings present an integrated systems genetics framework connecting naturally occurring genetic variation to quantitative disease phenotypes.

items.title_en: A comprehensive identification protocol for postcranial bones of Southeast Asian Ruminantia. Part 3: Morphological criteria for large-sized species
items.title_zh: 东南亚反刍动物颅后骨骼的综合鉴定方案。第3部分：大型物种的形态学标准
items.abstract_en: Postcranial remains of large-bodied ruminants are abundant in the Late Quaternary record of continental Southeast Asia, yet their taxonomic attribution remains one of the least resolved problems in the zooarchaeology of this biodiversity-rich region. We address it here with an osteological identification protocol covering the six large ruminant species of the mainland: Bubalus bubalis, Bos javanicus, Bos sauveli, Bos gaurus, Budorcas taxicolor and Rusa unicolor, built from a comparative sample of 109 skeletons. A total of 148 discrete characters over 27 skeletal elements representing 442 states were defined on a restricted set of individuals, then scored across the entire sample. Most proved remarkably stable within taxa with 80.0% of the character/taxon combinations showing a dominant state at a frequency above 95%, and a substantial number of states occurred in a single family, subfamily, genus or species. Character combinations for taxonomic identification were then evaluated by the use of two supervised machine learning methods, a random forest model and a naive Bayes classifier at each of four taxonomic ranks. The two behaved almost identically, with mean accuracies of 95-94% for families, 93% for subfamilies, 89% for genera and 76% for species; only the three closely related and unevenly sampled species of Bos resisted consistent separation. The weighted naive Bayes models are distributed as a standalone web application in which any combination of states observed on a single element returns attribution probabilities for every rank. Together these results offer a transparent and statistically explicit alternative to expert judgement for the identification of Late Quaternary postcranial mammal remains, in Southeast Asia and elsewhere.

items.title_en: A comprehensive identification protocol for postcranial bones of Southeast Asian Ruminantia. Part 2: Morphological criteria for small and medium-sized species
items.abstract_en: The taxonomic identification of postcranial elements from small and medium-sized ruminants represents a significant challenge in zooarchaeological and Late Quaternary paleontological studies, particularly in biodiversity-rich regions such as continental Southeast Asia. This study presents a comprehensive osteological reference framework for the small and medium-sized Ruminantia of this region, based on a comparative sample of 228 specimens representing 14 species across three families (Bovidae, Cervidae, and Moschidae). Osteological characters were first described on a small initial specimen set and subsequently scored across the full sample. Although a small number of character states were found to be unique to specific taxa, most proved highly variable, limiting their individual identification potential. To address this, a Random Forest and a Naive Bayes classifier were applied to assess the discriminatory power of character combinations across four taxonomic ranks (Family, Subfamily, Genus, and Species) on independent bones. Both approaches performed similarly, achieving mean identification accuracies of 87-86% at the family level, 69% at the subfamily level, 50% at the genus level, and 35-33% at the species level. The Naive Bayes models were further deployed as an interactive web application, allowing users to perform bone identification based on any combination of observable character states from a single anatomical element. Our results highlight the limits of morphological identification of postcranial elements in this taxonomic and biogeographic context, while demonstrating that a transparent, reproducible, and statistically grounded approach can still represent a significant step forward for zooarchaeological and Late Quaternary paleontological studies in Southeast Asia and beyond.

items.title_en: A preclinical platform for focused ultrasound delivery from microplate to awake brain
items.abstract_en: Background. Focused ultrasound (FUS) has broad therapeutic potential, but its mechanisms of action are poorly understood. Preclinical FUS research enables rigorous interrogation of understudied parameters, but fragmented, single-purpose benchtop devices prevent standardized acoustic exposure across models. Objective. To describe a unified preclinical FUS platform for cell culture, ex vivo tissue, and awake stereotaxic in vivo delivery in one lightweight system, validated using glioblastoma as a disease model. Methods. We performed single-well FUS delivery to 96-well microplates, single-well delivery to freshly resected human glioblastoma tissue, and stereotaxic transcranial delivery to awake, head-fixed mice ambulating freely on a floating cage. Output was independently calibrated in free field, with measured microplate insertion loss. Pulsed low-intensity focused ultrasound (pLIFU) was applied to GL261-bearing mice, resected human glioblastoma, and macrophage cell lines. Results. Awake stereotaxic pLIFU produced acute tumor signal attenuation in GL261-bearing mice (mean log2 fold-change -1.66 versus +5.20 controls, p = 0.016) with bioluminescence evidence consistent with focal targeting. Ex vivo pLIFU produced directionally consistent immunophenotypic shifts in human glioblastoma (increased iNOS+, decreased Arg1+ populations). In vitro, pLIFU reduced CD80 on immunosuppressive macrophages to 73% of baseline in RAW 264.7 cells (p = 0.0008, n = 5) and 64% in THP-1 cells (p = 0.0006, n = 2), with MHC II upregulation in RAW 264.7 (ratio 1.65, p = 0.004) and ARG1 reduction in THP-1 (ratio 0.52, p = 0.0025). Conclusions. A unified preclinical FUS platform validated across in vitro, ex vivo, and awake in vivo applications enables stereotaxically guided transcranial FUS in awake, head-fixed mice ambulating in an exploratory manner during sonication, and single-well microplate treatments.

items.title_en: Individualized brain-body signatures of positive emotions revealed by large-scale multimodal neurophysiological recording
items.abstract_en: Using one of the most comprehensive multimodal biosensing datasets in affective research, densely sampled within individuals, we asked how emotions are instantiated in each person's brain and body. Four participants viewed 168 emotion-evoking videos during 128-channel EEG and 28 autonomic, ocular and facial recordings. Cross-validated elastic-net classifiers distinguished each of 15 positive and neutral emotions from baseline in every participant (mean accuracy 87-97%). We found that no emotion was predicted by a single marker and each reflected a multimodal ensemble of cortical and autonomic activity whose composition was largely person-specific. Yet physiology-derived groupings converged selectively with self-report; Interest-Awe-Amusement-Satisfaction and Entrancement-Aesthetic Appreciation recurred across individuals based on physiology. Across emotion groups, frontal and posterior delta, posterior alpha and electrodermal activity formed a shared backbone, plausibly reflecting affective and sensory engagement, whereas cardiovascular and facial signals varied between people. This framework yields individualized, objective neurophysiological indicators of emotion, potentially aiding personalized diagnosis.

items.title_en: Dose-dependent transcriptional responses of marine prokaryotes to Fe-rich colloids of glacial and non-glacial origin in the Kerguelen region (Southern Ocean)
items.abstract_en: The trace metal iron (Fe) plays a key role in regulating microbial carbon metabolism through complex processes. In ocean regions where Fe is potentially limiting, new Fe sources can significantly influence prokaryotic activity and growth, stimulating the microbially-mediated cycling of carbon. The accelerated melting of glaciers delivers large quantities of Fe-rich material to the ocean, but the bioavailability of the diverse glacial Fe species remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the response of marine prokaryotes to Fe contained in the colloidal fraction (20 - 200 nm size fraction) originating from the Cook Ice Cap on Kerguelen Island (Southern Ocean). We assessed growth and gene transcriptional responses to dose-additions of Fe-rich colloids from two sources, glacial meltwater and a non-glacial origin. The two colloid types resulted both in dose-dependent, but contrasting growth responses. While non-glacial colloids stimulated prokaryotic growth, the opposite pattern was observed with glacial colloids. The transcriptional profiles revealed an increasing trend in Fe-limitation, as evidenced by transcripts of the glyoxylate shunt, as a function of the addition of either colloid type. However, only non-glacial colloids induced a dose-dependent increase in transcripts of aromatic compound degradation, suggesting that these Fe-rich colloids could also provide C. These results point to the key role of C regulating the prokaryotic growth in response to Fe-rich colloids. The clear trends in the expression of genes in response to dose addition allowed to map transcript abundances to nutritional stress and specific metabolic pathways. Dose additions of limiting nutrients in incubation experiments induce quantitative transcriptional responses, thereby offering insights to the nutritional status of prokaryotes and to the mechanisms leading to Fe and C co-limitation.

items.title_en: Indigenous Yanomami gut microbiota protects against diet-induced metabolic dysfunction
items.abstract_en: Industrialization profoundly alters the human gut microbiota, reducing microbial diversity and eliminating taxa prevalent in non-industrialized populations. These microbiota alterations accompanying industrialization might contribute to the increasing prevalence of obesity and other chronic inflammatory diseases, yet direct experimental evidence remains lacking. We compared the gut microbiota of Indigenous Brazilian Yanomami and urban Belgian donors and transplanted these into germ-free (GF) mice subjected to high-fat diet (HFD). The Yanomami microbiota exhibited greater richness and distinct composition enriched for VANISH (Volatile and/or Associated Negatively with Industrialized Societies of Humans) taxa. Transplantation of Yanomami microbiota significantly attenuated HFD-induced metabolic dysfunction, reducing weight gain, diabetes incidence, and promoting adipose and hepatic Th2 immunity. Yanomami-derived microbial communities displayed enhanced ecological stability and enrichment for short-chain fatty acid-associated taxa and metabolic functions post-HFD. Our findings demonstrate that the microbiota from low-urbanization populations confer protection against diet-induced metabolic disease, highlighting ecological resilience and specific microbial functions as potential targets for microbiota-inspired therapeutics.

items.title_en: Impact of HIV-1 infection on the microglia transcriptome: induction of microRNA-23b leads to G3BP2-mediated stress granules assembly disruption
items.abstract_en: Microglia act as HIV reservoirs in the brain and contribute to the development of HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders despite antiretroviral therapy. We examined the transcriptome of primary microglia infected ex vivo with HIV-1. Analyses reveal a significant modulation of DNA damage/cell cycle-, cellular stress- and non-membrane bounded organelle assembly-related gene expression, and a broad effect on the microRNA profile. MicroRNA-23b is identified among upregulated microRNAs in HIV-1-infected microglia, and downregulated g3bp2 mRNA, validated as its target. G3BP2 is a core component of stress granules (SGs), which serve as antiviral and proinflammatory platforms. MicroRNA-23b mimics reduced both G3BP2 expression and SG assembly in stress-induced monocyte-derived microglial cells (MDMi), and few SGs aggregate in infected MDMi. Inhibition of MicroRNA-23b partially re-established SG formation and reduced HIV-1 replication. Thus, microRNA-23b induction contributes to HIV-1 strategies aimed at counteracting SG assembly in infected microglia, a host response that restricts HIV-1 replication and ensuing neuropathogenesis.

items.title_en: Mechanistic insights into coronavirus inhibition by a distinct base-modified adenosine analog targeting the viral polymerase
items.abstract_en: Nucleoside analog (NA) inhibitors of viral polymerases are a chemically diverse and prominent class of antivirals, with most agents bearing sugar modifications to induce chain termination. Compounds with a modified base yet natural ribose are comparatively rare and typically incorporated to act as virus mutagens, raising significant safety concerns. How nucleobase modifications interfere with polymerization and the molecular basis of this effect remain poorly understood. We here define the mechanism of 6-ethyl-modified 7-deazaadenosine (EDA), a recently identified coronavirus (CoV) inhibitor that does not induce virus mutagenesis. Its strong activity spans across multiple CoVs and cell models and is dictated by the 6-ethyl substituent, with poor tolerance for smaller, larger or heteroatom-containing substituents. At the level of SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), EDA-triphosphate incorporates as a mimic of ATP but not other NTPs, inducing immediate stalling but also excision by the viral 3'-to-5' exonuclease. While EDA incorporation prevents extension with a second EDA residue, the stalling of natural NTP incorporation is transient and still allows the formation of longer products. A similar phenomenon is observed with template-embedded EDA. Cryo-EM analysis with SARS-CoV-2 RdRp revealed that 3'-terminal EDA is accommodated without distortion of the template:primer duplex, but its 6-ethyl group induces rearrangements in the NTP binding pocket that prevent stable binding of the incoming nucleotide. The mechanistic findings were validated through antiviral studies with SARS-CoV-2 mutants bearing core substitutions in the RdRp or exonuclease. Together, these findings position EDA as a mechanistically distinct base-modified NA prototype that has relevance beyond coronaviruses and underscores the ever-expanding versatility of NA-based polymerase inhibitors.

items.title_en: Complementing Biosafety Levels With Societal Safety Levels
items.abstract_en: Biosafety level (BSL) classifications of biological agents have succeeded at minimizing occupational risk inside laboratories, but largely neglect the potential for onward transmission. As a result, many non-transmissible pathogens that could kill at most one individual per person exposed require greater containment than 1918 influenza, a virus that killed 50-100 million and might cause a new pandemic today. Laboratory workers are consenting professionals; the public is not. We recommend complementing BSLs with explicit thresholds for expected societal harm. Here we formalize Societal Safety Levels (SSLs) based on expected public fatalities per year, which we quantify from (i) estimated probability of laboratory release, (ii) likelihood of societal transmission, and (iii) consequence. SSLs would apply specifically to laboratory research with replication-competent potential pandemic pathogens, and would not restrict field surveillance, sequencing, or countermeasure development using non-replicating systems or pandemic-incapable agents. We find that applying the 0.1 expected deaths per facility-year standard common across multiple major-hazard industries to potential pandemic pathogen research would require marked safety improvements. Complementing BSLs with SSLs would establish enforceable accident-safety thresholds for pandemic-capable pathogens, bringing high-risk biological research into alignment with the quantitative safety standards that help other hazardous industries operate with public acceptance.

items.title_en: Cancers relax selection on charge at the mitochondrial complex I quinone cavity
items.abstract_en: Mitochondrial complex I translocates protons through hydrated channels whose connectivity and electrostatics are both defined by structure, but whether they are distinctly constrained is unknown. From a 2.39 cryo-EM structure modelling 2,945 ordered waters, we built the proton wire of the seven mtDNA-encoded ND subunits and scored all 40,166 missense substitutions on two near-orthogonal axes (r = 0.17): electrostatic shift at proton-loading sites, and topological disruption of the wire. Across 858 germline variant sites, loading sites (0.51) and cut vertices (0.67) are both depleted. In tumours only loading sites are enriched (1.42 TCGA, 1.67 PCAWG, 1.29 MSK-IMPACT), a 3.06-fold difference tested as a wire class tissue-type interaction (P = 3.6 10-). It survives adjustment for conservation, burial and coverage, and is concentrated in ND1 within 15 of the quinone cavity, not spread along the proton path. Selection separates charge from connectivity, without establishing a fitness benefit.

items.title_en: Phase Separation of Intracellular Proteins Influences Synaptic Bistability
items.abstract_en: Synaptic bistability at the post synaptic density has been proposed to be the result of the nucleation and evaporation of receptor clusters. The exact biophysical mechanism underlying these inter-receptor attractions that can trigger nucleation remains to be elucidated. Emerging evidence demonstrates that numerous postsynaptic density submembrane proteins, that interact with various membrane receptors, can undergo phase separation, necessitating a revised conceptual model. By employing Langevin dynamics simulations of coarse-grained scaffold proteins and interacting membrane receptors, we study how phase transitions of scaffold proteins alter receptor clustering at the membrane. In our model, scaffold macromolecules can undergo phase separation and interact with receptor molecules at the model membranes. We observed that the presence of scaffold polymers across the membrane creates an attractive interaction between otherwise purely repulsive receptors. By systematically varying the number of receptors at the membrane, we dissected the coupling between receptor clustering and the phase behavior of scaffold macromolecules. We show that the propensity for receptor clustering is enhanced by the condensation of scaffold proteins. We then used two different scaffolds and systematically varied the interaction between them, to change the spatial organization of two condensed phases w.r.t. one another. Interestingly, we observed that receptor clustering can be reduced by co-phase separation of scaffold macromolecules, indicating the role of competing interactions in receptor clustering. Our work advances understanding of receptor-mediated signaling and phase separation, providing insights into cellular compartmentalization and biochemical regulation at the synapse.

items.title_en: Executive and language systems competitively shape predictive processing during reading
items.abstract_en: When we read, our brains constantly generate predictions about upcoming words, which is thought to make comprehension faster and more efficient. Yet it remains unclear whether this predictive mechanism relies on the same domain-general executive resources the brain uses for other demanding cognitive tasks, or operates largely independently within the language system. Here we tested this question using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in twenty-five healthy adults, who performed self-paced naturalistic reading, an n-back task, and a dual task of concurrent reading and n-back, allowing us to place competing demands on cognitive resources. In three sessions, we stimulated the left angular gyrus alone, the angular gyrus together with dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, a hub of executive control, or delivered sham stimulation, and used computational modeling of decision-making to isolate how each brain state altered the underlying cognitive processes. Combined stimulation of the angular gyrus and prefrontal cortex selectively weakened the reading-time costs of unexpected words, but only when reading competed with the working-memory task, revealing that linguistic prediction draws on executive resources specifically under cognitive load. Computational models showed that the relationship was bidirectional: Unpredictable words also disrupted concurrent working-memory decisions, slowing the accumulation of evidence and increasing response caution. Together, these findings show that predictive language processing is not a fixed, encapsulated function but is dynamically coupled to executive control when cognitive demands compete. Our results provide evidence that prediction during language comprehension is embedded within a broader, demand-sensitive cognitive architecture that flexibly coordinates linguistic and executive resources.

items.title_en: Genomic Potential vs. Pathogenic Reality: Functional Virulence Variation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
items.abstract_en: Despite the rapid expansion of bacterial genome sequencing, predicting pathogen virulence from genomic information remains a major challenge. To study this association, we integrate comparative genomics, functional phenotyping, host-pathogen interaction assays, and infection outcomes across a diverse collection of 28 Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, representing clinically relevant diversity in serotype, type IV pilus group, and flagellar type. While virulence-associated systems were broadly retained across the strain collection, isolates displayed substantial variation in phenotypic behavior and pathogenicity. Genotypic classifications based on pilus, flagellar, siderophore, or secretion system characteristics were poor predictors of virulence-associated phenotypes. Pathogenicity in a Galleria mellonella model varied markedly among strains and was most strongly associated with surface-associated motility, whereas other virulence traits and quorum-sensing genotypes showed limited predictive value. In a three-dimensional lung epithelial cell model, inflammatory responses were negatively correlated with activity of the type III secretion system effector ExoS, suggesting a role in modulation of host immune signaling. Together, these findings demonstrate that virulence emerges from functional deployment of conserved virulence repertoires, rather than their mere presence. By linking genomic diversity to phenotypic expression, pathogenicity, and host responses within a single strain collection, this study highlights fundamental limitations of gene-content-based virulence prediction and underscores the importance of integrating genomic and functional data to better understand P. aeruginosa virulence.

items.title_en: ART: A Compositional Physical Theory for the End-to-End Design of Solid-Phase Immunosensors
items.abstract_en: Predicting complete solid phase immunoassay performance remains challenging because antibody recognition, reactor transport, molecular transduction and physical observation are coupled rather than independent. Here, we formulate ART as a compositional physical theory expressed as Y = Ts[Tm[AR(X)]]. Recognition A and reactor transport R jointly determine the retained molecular state, while molecular transduction Tm and physical observation Ts operate through replaceable interfaces. Finite-time kinetic and reaction diffusion calculations across plate, tubular and bead formats show that antibodies with identical dissociation constants can produce different capture responses because of distinct association and dissociation rates. In fixed-length tubular reactors, mass-conserving transport distinguishes surface capture density from fractional recovery, revising a first-passage-based local density optimum while preserving a multicriterion design window. An AR-only concentration-threshold map identifies when recognition kinetics or reactor redesign offers greater local leverage. The benefits of improved affinity also depend on the kinetic pathway and reactor regime. For enzymatic transduction, we propose a four-parameter, substrate-conserving model in which the saturation-shape parameter is hm = KM/S0 under a one effective substrate approximation. Accumulated TMB color and time-dependent luminol emission represent distinct consequences of reaction progress, while Ts describes measurement limits through a simplified floor slope roof model. ELISA with OD450 readout and tubular chemiluminescence with camera detection illustrate the end-to-end framework. These examples remain conditional model demonstrations, and existing complete chain curves have not yet been recalibrated using the new enzyme model. ART provides a modular quantitative framework for assay design based on explicit physical interfaces and coupled processes.

items.title_en: Phylogenies can be used to predict future diversification but with limited success
items.abstract_en: Understanding the processes leading to the emergence of new lineages is one of the major tasks of macroevolution as a scientific field. Multiple commonly used models and metrics allow to estimate the rates of species diversification at the tips of phylogenetic trees, and are thus potentially useful for predicting future evolutionary success of individual extant lineages. However, the predictive performance of these methods has never been tested with real-world data. Here we use a new approach to quantify the relationship between predictor tip rates and subsequent diversification rates derived from a probability distribution of numbers of daughter species. We explore if and how well the tip-rate methods predict near-future diversification using temporal slices across large fossil and extant tetrapod phylogenies. We find that tip rate estimates from these methods do predict diversification in all four extant and one out of three fossil phylogenies. The quality of these predictions varies across the tested methods, with the model-free approach being more robust overall but likelihood-based models delivering correctly scaled diversification rates. Our results suggest that future cladogenesis can be predicted using existing tip rate methods, but only moderately well and likely dependant on factors that are difficult to evaluate in practical applications.

items.title_en: Multi-resolution humanness scoring of antibodies via a region-isolated language model
items.title_zh: 通过区域隔离语言模型对抗体进行多分辨率人源性评分
items.abstract_en: Antibodies recognized as foreign can elicit anti-drug antibodies that compromise efficacy and safety, making humanness scoring, estimating how human-like a sequence appears, an early, repeated step in antibody development. Widely used scores reduce a variable domain to a single framework-dominated number, leaving the complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) grafted during humanization, diversified by generative models weakly supervised and rarely audited. Here we introduce IgScope, a 23-million-parameter antibody language model trained from scratch that scores humanness at chain, IMGT-region, and residue resolution; a region-isolated attention module confines attention to within-region pairs, and chimeric-sequence training supplies region-level supervision. On 2.38 million held-out chains, masking all framework tokens leaves CDR accuracy unchanged, and back-mutated murine residues in human frameworks are detected at 93.4% accuracy. At chain level, IgScope matches the strongest published correlation with clinical anti-drug-antibody incidence (r = 0.567, n = 217) and outperforms a same-protocol recomputation. Region-level scoring exposes what chain-level scoring conceals: antibodies designed de novo by four generative models pass whole-chain humanness (0.966-0.988), while their CDRs score far below natural (P < 1e-30) in every chain class. Quality control turns the same resolution to the mirror-image question: in humanized-mouse platforms, whose domains are human by design, IgScope scores the domain as human and, in HUGO-Nano chimeric VHHs, isolates only the FR2 signal of four camelid hallmark residues deliberately retained to stabilize the VHH. IgScope gives antibody humanization a verified foundation and generative design an audit.

items.title_en: Single molecule studies of the bacterial curli protein CsgA reveal a structurally dynamic monomeric structure
items.title_zh: 细菌curli蛋白CsgA的单分子研究揭示了一种结构动态的单体结构
items.abstract_en: E. coli curli, an archetypical bacterial amyloid, is a critical biofilm scaffold comprised mainly of the CsgA protein. CsgA is highly aggregation prone, confounding high-resolution studies of its structure and amyloid formation mechanism. Ensemble studies show that monomeric CsgA is intrinsically disordered, while structure predictions show a well-folded {beta}-solenoid. Here, single-molecule force spectroscopy with optical tweezers is used to define the conformational dynamics in single CsgA molecules. CsgA monomer shows unfolding/refolding consistent with fully folded, partially folded and collapsed molten globule conformations, indicating that CsgA exists in metastable folded states in equilibrium with disordered states. These folded states are likely highly aggregation prone and thus have avoided characterization at the ensemble level.
